significance: A goddess shrine near Jadugora whose object of worship is a stone taken to be Rankini herself; the present building was put up between 1947 and 1950 after Dinbandhu Singh began the worship, and a family trust has run it since 1954. Originally a Bhumij tribal cult, it saw human sacrifice until the British stopped the practice around 1865.
story: The goddess is said to have taken the form of a girl fleeing a shepherd who hid in a washerman's bundle of clothes at Kapadgadi Ghat, whereupon the pile of cloth turned to stone.
